newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DEVILS TAKE 3-0 LEAD OVER CANADIENS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DEVILS TAKE 3-0 LEAD OVER CANADIENS.

text.p: The New Jersey Devils, behind Valeri Zelepukin's hat trick, beat the Montreal Canadiens 6-4 to take a 3-0 lead in their Eastern Conference quarterfinal series on Tuesday.

In the other Eastern Conference best-of-seven series, the New York Rangers rallied in overtime on the strength of Esa Tikkanen's rocket goal to beat the Florida Panthers 4-3 for a 2-1 lead in their playoff duel.
In the Western Conference, all four games ended with the series tied 2-2.

The Chicago Blackhawks beat the Colorado Avalanche 6-3, the St Louis Blues blanked the Detroit Red Wings 4-0, the Dallas Stars edged the Edmonton Oilers 4-3 and the Phoenix Coyotes shut out the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim 2-0.
In Montreal, rookie Patrik Elias and Bobby Holik each had a goal and an assist for New Jersey, which can eliminate the Canadiens on Thursday with a win in Game Four at Montreal.
"We can play a bit more patient and we really didn't do that," New Jersey defenceman Scott Stevens said.
Mark Recchi scored his first two playoff goals for the Canadiens, who have been swept in a best-of-seven series only once in the last 45 years.
Zelepukin had scored only one goal in his previous 20 post-season games, but scored twice Tuesday in a 2:17 span in the second period to give New Jersey its first lead, 4-3.
"It's like playing the Russian Red Army team, the most famous team on Earth. You don't need to pick up your confidence to play them. You always play Montreal on the top of your game," Zelepukin said.

Tikkanen's winning goal for the Rangers was hit so hard it blasted off the camera in the back of the Florida net and came back out so fast that officials had to review replays before signalling the goal was good.

The Panthers appeared to have a victory in the bank when Luc Robitaille scored his second goal of the game off a furious goalmouth scramble with 18.9 second left in regulation to send the game into overtime.

The Rangers had been thoroughly outplayed over the second and third periods, but all the Panthers good work -- including erasing a 2-0 deficit with three second-period goals -- was nullified in those last frantic seconds of regulation.
In Chicago, Bob Probert scored twice in a four-goal second period and Tony Amonte had two goals and an assist in their victory over the Avalanche.
Rookies Ethan Moreau and Steve Dubinsky also scored in the second period for the Blackhawks, who had more goals in this game than the first three games of the series combined.
Keith Jones and Joe Sakic scored in the first period to stake Colorado to a 2-1 lead.
"We never gave up," Amonte said. "We know they are the Stanley Cup champions, but we're not going to quit. We just need a big effort in Colorado."
In St Louis, Grant Fuhr recorded his second shutout of the series and fifth in the post-season and Geoff Courtnall scored twice, to lead the Blues past Detroit.
Fuhr, who blanked Detroit, 2-0, in Game One, made 28 saves for his 80th career post-season victory, tying him with Ken Dryden for third on the all-time list.
Brett Hull and Pavol Demitra each scored a goal and set up two others and Chris Pronger also tallied for the Blues.
Detroit went 0-for-5 on the power play and is 2-for-28 in the series.
In Edmonton, Brent Gilchrist's goal 1:53 into the third period snapped a tie, allowing Dallas to escape with their 4-3 victory.
The Stars nearly squandered a 4-2 lead in the final 73 seconds of this contest.
"This game was more of an Oilers' game in terms of tempo," said Dallas coach Ken Hitchcock. "They run on emotion, and if you let them loose, they'll kill you."
Jamie Langenbrunner added what proved to be the winning goal with 14:39 left for Dallas, which also received a goal and an assist from Mike Modano.
Jason Arnott had a goal and two assists and Ryan Smyth added a goal and an assist for Edmonton.

In Phoenix, Nikolai Khabibulin posted his first career playoff shutout and Bob Corkum's goal with 7:15 left in regulation broke a scoreless tie to give the Phoenix Coyotes the 2-0 whitewash of the Ducks.
Khabibulin stopped 32 shots and has allowed only one goal in the last two games after giving up six in the first two.
Corkum's goal came 47 seconds after an apparent goal by Anaheim's Steve Rucchin was disallowed.
Teppo Numminen added an empty-net goal with six seconds left to cap the victory.
